content.title: Masters 2026 leaderboard: Rory McIlroy grabs early share of the lead after Thursday at Augusta National
content.text: The 90th edition of the Masters is officially here … and Rory McIlroy picked up right where he left off.After a sluggish start, the defending Masters champion carded five birdies in an eight-hole stretch to get himself to 5-under for the tournament and into the clubhouse lead alongside Sam Burns.AdvertisementFor McIlroy, it’s quite a difference from a year ago, when he left Round 1 seven shots back of Justin Rose, who he would eventually beat in a playoff that Sunday.“I think a fair score for me today would have been like 2-under maybe with some of the places I hit it,” McIlroy said after, an acknowledgement that he didn’t actually play that well for the first seven holes. “But again, I used my head and I didn't — I got up-and-down when I needed to. I didn't compound mistakes. Again, that's just a learning curve that you have to go through around here, and I did it well today.”This is now the first time that McIlroy has led overnight at Augusta National since 2011. Of course, that’s a tournament he’d rather forget. He was the leader after the first three rounds, held a four-shot lead heading into Sunday’s final round, only to implode at No. 10 en route to an 8-over 80.He was only 21 then. Now, at 36, has a lot more experience, plus a green jacket.Follow along with Yahoo Sports for the latest updates and highlights from Round 1 of the 2026 Masters:Live coverage is over46 updatesThu, April 9, 2026 at 1:01 PM UTCJay HartPositionPlayerScoreThruT1.Sam Burns-5FT1.Rory McIlroy-5FT3.Patrick Reed-3FT3.Kurt Kitayama-3FT3.Jason Day-3FT6.Xander Schauffele-2FT6.Justin Rose-2FT6.Shane Lowry-2FT6.Scottie Scheffler-2FThu, April 9, 2026 at 11:19 PM UTCScottie Scheffler missed some prime birdie opportunities down the stretch, settling for pars that should have been better. And still he’s -2, just three shots off the lead.Scheffler will no doubt be scuffling about his round, but he remains in contention yet again at Augusta National, where history dictates you pretty much have to be in the top 10 after Round 1 to win on Sunday.Thu, April 9, 2026 at 10:50 PM UTCJay HartAfter getting to within one shot of the lead, Justin Rose finished bogey-bogey to drop to -2. Not a great finish, but a solid round for last year’s runner-up.Thu, April 9, 2026 at 10:31 PM UTCJay HartWith birdies at 15 and 17, Brooks Koepka has got it to -1.It’s been a bit since the once major collector has been in contention at a major, really not since he won at the 2023 PGA.He’s currently tied for 11th.Thu, April 9, 2026 at 10:26 PM UTCRyan YoungRobert MacIntyre went into the water on 15 just now, and he flipped off the hole from the fairway. Forget Bryson’s bunker meltdown, this may be the most relatable thing all day.MacIntyre would go on to card a 9 at the hole, which pretty much ends his Masters.Thu, April 9, 2026 at 10:04 PM UTCRyan YoungWell, he’s one off the lead again. Justin Rose reached the par 5 15th in two just now, and had a very simple two-putt birdie to get back within range of McIlroy and Burns.He’s not going away anytime soon.Thu, April 9, 2026 at 9:53 PM UTCDan WolkenAfter shooting 67 for the co-lead on a day where his game wasn’t nearly that good, Rory might be as dangerous as ever as he tries to become the first golfer since Tiger Woods in 2001-02 to win back-to-back here.“I feel like the way I played, 5-under sort of exceeded where I thought I would be or what I wanted to do,” he said. “I think a fair score for me today would have been like 2-under maybe with some of the places I hit it. But again, I used my head and got up-and-down when I needed to. I didn't compound mistakes. Again, that's just a learning curve that you have to go through around here, and I did it well today.”Rory McIlroy entered the clubhouse with a share of the lead Thursday at Augusta. (Andrew Redington/Getty Images) (Andrew Redington via Getty Images)Thu, April 9, 2026 at 9:37 PM UTCRyan YoungWell, Justin Rose’s bogey-free run is over. He followed up his birdie at the 13th with a bogey, and he’s now two back again.He’s still very much in contention (it’s only Thursday afternoon, after all) but will need a big finish if he’s going to catch the leaders tonight.Thu, April 9, 2026 at 9:19 PM UTCThis really feels like a repeat of last year.Justin Rose just birdied the 13th, and now trails Rory McIlroy (and Sam Burns) by just a single shot as he enters the final stretch of the golf course.Thu, April 9, 2026 at 9:16 PM UTCCorey Conners really needed this one. He was 3-over on the back nine alone before this wild birdie.He’ll still have to fight to make the cut, but this was a huge save.Thu, April 9, 2026 at 8:52 PM UTCJay BusbeeAUGUSTA, Ga. — One year ago, Bryson DeChambeau held the solo lead at the Masters on Sunday. After his very next round at Augusta National, he was nine strokes behind the clubhouse leader, looking for answers from an unforgiving course. And not even his homemade club could keep his card clean.DeChambeau finished his first day at the 2026 Masters at 4-over, far behind clubhouse leaders Sam Burns and Rory McIlroy (-5). After his round, a visibly frustrated DeChambeau nonetheless spoke to the media. His normally analytical mind was spinning its wheels in mud, trying to figure out how everything had gone so wrong so quickly.“Everybody has an ability for weird things to happen,” DeChambeau said in a short postround interview, “and today I just did not have my irons under control, which is weird.”For more on DeChambeau’s first round, and his 3-D printed 5 iron, click here.Bryson DeChambeau carried a 3-D printed 5 iron in his bag on Thursday at the Masters. Adam Scott nearly did one better:Alas, he had to settle for ONLY an eagle, but it did put him in red figures at -1.Thu, April 9, 2026 at 8:04 PM UTCJay HartWoodland has got it to -3, and if you don’t know his story, it is absolutely insane.A few years ago, Woodland had brain surgery to remove a lesion. Scary stuff. But it gets worse. Ever since, Woodland has suffered from PTSD, to the point where he has visions of people trying to kill him. He felt it during the second round of the Houston Open a couple weeks ago as he walked the course. It’s absolutely terrifying and heartbreaking at the same time,But then … he went on to win that tournament, which qualified him for this Masters, and here he is on the first page of the leaderboard.You can read Woodland’s story here.Thu, April 9, 2026 at 7:49 PM UTCA year ago, McIlroy ended Round 1 seven shots back of the lead. This year, he’s in a much better position, finishing off with a 67, putting him in a tie with Sam Burns for the clubhouse lead.Sounds great, right?Well, yes, until you remember the only other time he held the lead after Round 1 was 2011, when he infamously gave up a massive lead on Sunday to let the green jacket slip away and ultimately elude him for more than a decade.Thu, April 9, 2026 at 7:47 PM UTCJay HartLudvig Åberg is the popular pick to win his first major, and he had it going through eight holes. But at the ninth, well, the wheels came off a bit. After putting his drive into the pine straw, Åberg had to scramble and wound up with a double, dropping him from -3 to -1.Thu, April 9, 2026 at 7:41 PM UTCJay HartConsidering where DeChambeau sits, let’s dig into how the Masters cutline works, which is quite simple: Top 50 and ties make it to the weekend.DeChambeau, at +4, currently sits T63.Othere big names on the wrong side as of now include Jon Rahm (+3) and Bubba Watson (+4).Thu, April 9, 2026 at 7:31 PM UTCRyan YoungIf he didn’t have that bunker meltdown on No. 11, Bryson DeChambeau wouldn’t be in a terrible spot. But with that triple bogey, and a bogey at the 18th after he missed a long par save, DeChambeau is now at 4-over.He’s going to have to work to make the cut on Friday.Thu, April 9, 2026 at 7:00 PM UTCRyan YoungMake it three straight for Rory McIlroy now after his birdie at the 15th. He pulled the latest one off after sending his drive on the par-5 way off to the left into the trees, too.McIlroy’s tied with Burns at 5-under with a real chance to take the clubhouse lead.Thu, April 9, 2026 at 6:36 PM UTCRyan YoungScottie Scheffler just drove the green at the par-4 third after his eagle, which left him with a very easy two-putt birdie.He’s only two off the lead now with 15 holes to go today. Scheffler appears to be on a mission today.
